prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
The document sets five missions: sustained economic growth; clean power by 2030; safer communities; wider opportunity through childcare, education and skills; and a modernised health and care system. It anchors policy to fiscal rules: day‑to‑day spending balanced by revenues and debt falling as a share of GDP in year five, with all major fiscal events independently forecast. It pledges no rises to National Insurance, or basic, higher or additional Income Tax rates, or VAT; funds reforms partly via tackling tax avoidance, abolishing non‑dom status, closing loopholes, and modernising HMRC.

Economy and growth
- A statutory Industrial Strategy Council; sector plans (e.g., automotive, life sciences, creative industries); a 10‑year infrastructure strategy and a National Infrastructure and Service Transformation Authority.
- A National Wealth Fund (£7.3bn) to catalyse private investment in ports, gigafactories, steel, carbon capture and green hydrogen; pension reform to boost UK investment.
- Business tax roadmap; corporation tax capped at 25% for the parliament; permanent full expensing; replace business rates in England.
- Planning reform to build 1.5m homes, restore mandatory housing targets, prioritise brownfield, strategic “grey belt” release with safeguards, new towns, more social and affordable homes, and a permanent mortgage guarantee for first‑time buyers.
- Deeper devolution in England with statutory Local Growth Plans and multi‑year settlements for councils.
- Employment law reform: ban exploitative zero‑hours contracts and “fire and rehire,” day‑one rights to parental leave, sick pay and unfair dismissal protection; a Single Enforcement Body; minimum wage to reflect cost of living and removal of lower adult age bands.
- Immigration system tied to skills and training, stronger enforcement against abuse, and workforce plans in sectors with shortages.

Clean energy, climate and nature
- Zero‑carbon electricity by 2030 by doubling onshore wind, tripling solar, and quadrupling offshore wind; investment in CCS, hydrogen, marine energy and long‑duration storage; maintain a strategic gas reserve; no new coal or new oil and gas exploration licences; extend and tighten the windfall levy.
- A public energy company (Great British Energy) capitalised with £8.3bn to co‑invest and scale local generation; grid and market reform with stronger regulation and lower standing charges.
- Warm Homes Plan: £6.6bn to upgrade five million homes; higher private‑rented efficiency standards by 2030.
- Clean water enforcement, tougher fines and executive accountability; habitat expansion, new National River Walks and National Forests; support for farming with greener procurement targets and a land‑use framework; stronger animal welfare.

Public services and safety
- Health: 40,000 extra weekly appointments by extended hours and pooled waiting lists; use spare independent capacity; double CT/MRI scanners; New Hospitals Programme; an innovation and adoption strategy; enhanced NHS app; more GPs, face‑to‑face guarantees, continuity of care; community pharmacist prescribing; a Dentistry Rescue Plan (700,000 urgent appointments) and contractual reform; 8,500 additional mental‑health staff; modernised Mental Health Act; public‑health measures on smoking, youth vaping, junk‑food advertising and energy drinks.
- Social care: a National Care Service with national standards, “home first,” a Fair Pay Agreement, and closer NHS‑care integration.
- Policing and justice: a Neighbourhood Policing Guarantee with thousands of additional officers/PCSOs/special constables funded by efficiencies; new Respect Orders; tougher action on shoplifting and assaults on retail workers; a knife‑crime plan with mandatory interventions and bans on certain blades; Young Futures hubs nationwide; specialist rape units and courts; stronger police vetting and misconduct rules; court backlog measures; prison capacity expansion and a reoffending reduction programme; strategic review of probation; action on historical injustices.

Children, education and skills
- 3,000 school‑based nurseries; free breakfast clubs in every primary; 6,500 new teachers in shortage subjects; curriculum and assessment review; SEND inclusion; school inspection reform to multi‑metric report cards; mental‑health professionals in every school.
- Skills England; devolution of adult skills; transform FE into Technical Excellence Colleges; replace the Apprenticeship Levy with a flexible Growth and Skills Levy; sustain university access and stabilise sector finances.

Governance and international
- An independent Ethics and Integrity Commission; tighter rules on ministerial conduct; restrictions on second jobs for MPs; immediate Lords reforms (end hereditary voting, mandatory retirement at 80) and consultation on a more representative second chamber; votes at 16; improved voter registration.
- Reset intergovernmental relations across the UK; a Council of the Nations and Regions; tailored arrangements for Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland.
- Security: Strategic Defence Review and path to 2.5% of GDP; unwavering NATO and nuclear deterrent commitments; veteran support; defence industrial strategy and procurement reform; steadfast support for Ukraine; strategic China policy.
- Trade: targeted agreements and sector deals; improved EU cooperation without re‑entering the single market, customs union or freedom of movement; global minimum corporate tax support.
- Development: rebuild capacity with a mission to end poverty on a liveable planet; restore 0.7% ODA when fiscal conditions allow.
- Climate diplomacy: lead a Clean Power Alliance to accelerate global energy transition.
